newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada, United States to resume stalled salmon talks.
newsitem.headline: Canada, United States to resume stalled salmon talks.

text.p: The United States and Canada were scheduled on Wednesday to resume contentious talks over dividing the Pacific salmon catch after a collapse in negotiations last month.
Negotiators for the two countries were due to meet in a Vancouver suburb early Wednesday evening for the first time since May 21.
The Canadians walked out of that meeting in Seattle, saying the lead U.S. negotiator was not authorised to offer a specific catch reduction.

Canada suspended the negotiations and accused the United States of bargaining in bad faith. That prompted a war of words between the two countries and it took several weeks of diplomatic efforts to get negotiations back on track.

Canada's Fisheries Minister David Anderson told reporters in Vancouver late Tuesday that he hoped for a deal this week. "We expect the negotiations to go well," he said. "We're optimistic, cautiously optimistic."
The two neighbours have squabbled for years over how to divide dwindling salmon stocks in the Pacific Northwest and several attempts at a settlement have failed.
But pressure is mounting for a deal soon as the salmon fishing season gets underway. Officials are expected to meet for three days this week.

Hopes grew after Anderson met Alaska Gov. Tony Knowles in Juneau, Alaska, on Tuesday. Alaska has historically been a holdout in the negotiations but after the meeting Knowles called the dispute a "very solveable issue."

British Columbia Premier Glen Clark called the resumption of talks positive but remained wary. "It's clearly a good sign ... but frankly I just don't trust the Americans after four years of screwing around on this," he told reporters.
Clark has announced plans to cancel the lease on an underwater military testing range used by U.S. submarines in hopes of pressuring the United States into a deal.

When the talks broke down last month Canada annonuced it would begin enforcing existing rules that require U.S. fishing boats in its waters to report to Canadian authorities. The Canadian Coast Guard temporarily seized four boats under that policy, a move that angered the United States.
Canada has threatened to consider other measures against the United States if no deal is reached including imposing a transit fee on U.S. fishboats as it did in 1994.
